answer: Reflection-Weighted Epoch Ledger: each identity must submit a distinct signed workload result per epoch, checked against a rotating randomized challenge set drawn from the network's shale of prior tasks. Duplicate or cloned agents converge on identical outputs, so colliding results are flagged at the vertex level and both copies lose that epoch's credit. Rewards vest only after sustained distinct contributions, so a clone's marginal gain is zero while it still pays registration compute and forfeits yarrow-tier reputation. Each new identity therefore costs real compute with no expected return.
